featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Lakmé Salon, Churchgate (near Eros Theatre) for a simple hair wash and blow dry, for which the charge was 1100. From the very beginning, the experience was downhill.

During the hair wash, I was asked whether I wanted a “normal shampoo” or a “sulphate free shampoo”, and was told the sulphate free shampoo would cost an additional ₹450. This upselling at the wash station itself was extremely off-putting especially when they were charging 1100. Since I needed the service only for a single function, I agreed to the normal shampoo, expecting at least a decent wash.

The real disaster started during the blow dry. Anyone with basic training knows that curly hair should be blow-dried downwards to avoid frizz. Instead, the stylist blow-dried my hair in the worst possible way, turning it into a frizzy mess. When I pointed this out, instead of acknowledging his mistake, he blamed my hair for the result, essentially covering up his lack of skill.

For context, I get blow-dries twice a month, and this has never happened to me before. Moreover i get blowdries from not very big salons in thane and they do such a better job.

I complained to the manager, who again asked the person to “fix” my hair, but he only made it even more frizzy. As compensation, they offered a ₹200 discount, which honestly felt insulting considering I walked out looking embarrassing and completely dissatisfied. Net result: ₹900 wasted and a ruined look for my function.

To make matters worse, the general vibe of the salon was terrible as the staff looked uninterested, disengaged, and in a hurry to go home. There was zero concern for customer satisfaction; it felt purely transactional and money-driven.

To top it all off, the stylist missed an entire strand of hair while blow-drying, which is clearly visible in the photo I am attaching.

Please do NOT visit this salon if you have an important event or function. They do not value their customers, do not take responsibility for poor service, and definitely do not live up to the Lakmé brand name.

In a noble quest to earn those ever-elusive husband brownie points, I agreed to accompany my wife to Butterfly Pond Boutique Salon. This much-buzzed-about spot in South Bombay’s (SoBo) beauty scene is tucked away at Usha Sadan, Shop No. 1, right next to the Colaba Post Office. Promising a touch of pampering and luxury, it sounded like the perfect opportunity to make my wife happy (and rack up some “best husband” credentials).

The journey started off promising, with a breezy cab ride to Colaba. But the final stretch to the salon turned into a real-life version of Survivor. Think puddles, rogue chai stains, and paan spit markings so artistic they could rival street murals. I briefly questioned my life choices, but my wife reassured me with a smirk: “It’s the destination that matters, darling.” Easy for her to say.

While my wife was promptly ushered in for her blow-dry session, I decided to kill some time by strolling down Colaba Post Office Road, where nostalgia hit me like a kulfi on a summer day. There it was—an old milk stall from my childhood, now transformed into an air-conditioned sweet mart. I couldn’t resist stepping in, treating myself, and boring the shopkeeper with tales of the good old days. Feeling both old and satisfied, I returned to the salon.

Stepping inside Butterfly Pond was like stumbling into a parallel universe. Gone was the chaos outside; in its place was a tranquil oasis of modern interiors, soft lighting, and muted tones that screamed “zen.” I awkwardly parked myself in a plush lounge chair, only to spot another guy also caught in the waiting-game trap, flanked by his two boys. Misery, it turns out, loves company. We exchanged knowing nods—the universal signal of “we’re in this together, mate.”

The staff at Butterfly Pond? Absolute legends. A stylist walked up to us, flashing a smile that could melt butter, and kindly offered tea or coffee. She even pretended not to notice how out of place I looked, which I appreciated. Meanwhile, Ali Askari (my new BFF in salon purgatory) and I couldn’t help but joke about how we’d definitely be back… if only to stay in our wives’ good books a little longer.

As for cleanliness, Butterfly Pond nailed it. Every tool was sanitized, every surface spotless. My wife—who treats cleanliness as the Eighth Wonder of the World—was visibly impressed. I mentally bookmarked that moment, knowing it would come in handy for future arguments.

Now, let’s address the elephant in the room: the infamous entrance path. Honestly, it’s less “welcome to luxury” and more “watch your step.” But hey, once you’re inside, it’s smooth sailing. Whether you’re there for a transformation or just playing the supportive spouse, Butterfly Pond delivers on every front.

We walked out with my wife looking fabulous and me basking in the glow of newfound husband points. In other words, a highly successful mission.

🌟 Rating: 4.7/5 (minus 0.3 for the obstacle course outside—stay nimble, folks).
